messages:
alex: Brought up the SFO GPU rack earlier today. Need to run the performance validation runbook (driver/kernel checks, microbench, end-to-end throughput/latency). Posting checklist and commands.

alex: Checklist: 1) verify NVIDIA driver + CUDA, 2) check nvlink topology & ECC, 3) validate kernel modules and iommu settings, 4) run microbench (latency tokens/sec), 5) run 10m steady-state load, 6) capture perf counters & dmesg, 7) handoff doc updates.

maya: Thanks — can you paste the exact commands you want us to run for steps 1-3?

alex: Sure. Quick snaps to run on each node: 
```
# driver + cuda
nvidia-smi -q | egrep "Driver Version|CUDA Version|GPU Current Clock"
modinfo nvidia | head -n 20
uname -r
# topology / nvlink
nvidia-smi topo -m
# check mig (if A100)
nvidia-smi -L
```
Run as root or sudo. Collect outputs to the ticket.

todd: Ran on node sfo-rack-3-gpu-02, paste here: 
```
Driver Version: 535.86.10
CUDA Version: 12.1
GPU Current Clock: 1410 MHz
NVML Device 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB
Topology: NVLink peer 0-1: NVLink
```
Got no ECC errors.

maya: Good. Next: kernel module params and iommu. Commands: 
```
cat /proc/cmdline
dmesg | grep -i -e nvidia -e iommu -e "vfio"
lsmod | egrep "nvidia|nv_peer_mem|nvidia_uvm"
```
If iommu is off for this kernel we need to add intel_iommu=on, iommu=pt to grub for the private deployment nodes.

alex: Also check NIC config — we saw MTU/flow-control affecting RPC latencies previously. Run: 
```
ip link show dev eth0
ethtool -k eth0
ethtool -S eth0 | head
```
Set MTU 9000 on rack fabric and re-test if below baseline.

sam: For microbenchmarks, do you want us to use the usual perf-infer harness? Which model and sequence length?

alex: Use perf-infer v2 with the gpt-3.5-compat small shard we use in benchmarks. Two modes: 1) latency SLO test (single-stream, seq 512, batch 1, 1000 runs). 2) throughput steady-state (concurrent 16 streams, seq 2048, 10 min). Commands: 
```
./perf-infer --model /models/gpt35-compat --mode latency --seq 512 --runs 1000 --batch 1
./perf-infer --model /models/gpt35-compat --mode throughput --concurrency 16 --seq 2048 --duration 600
```
Collect p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.

todd: Started latency run on sfo-rack-3-gpu-02 -> p50 18ms, p95 62ms, p99 120ms, tokens/sec 3200 (single GPU). Baseline expected p95 <= 70ms so we're ok.

infra-bot: Automated kernel/driver checks completed for sfo-rack-3-gpu-* : all nodes report driver 535.86.10, CUDA 12.1. One node (sfo-rack-3-gpu-07) shows nv_peer_mem missing. Created ticket INFRA-1123.

maya: nv_peer_mem missing is likely dkms build failure after kernel update. For that node: run `dkms status` then reinstall nvidia-uvm: 
```
sudo dkms remove -m nvidia -v 535.86.10 --all || true
sudo dkms install -m nvidia -v 535.86.10
sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm
```
Then re-run lsmod.

sam: For steady-state throughput run I saw variance spikes when the autoscaler kicks. Please make sure autoscaler is disabled during the 10m runs or pin capacity.

alex: Good call. Disable autoscaling for the validation window and pin GPUs to the test pool. Also ensure no background node updates or cron jobs.

todd: Throughput run started on node group sfo-test-pool (4 x A100). Observed aggregate 12.6k tokens/sec steady for 10m with p95 latency 95ms. Previously in lab we saw 13.2k tokens/sec for same config — ~5% regression.

maya: Regression could be network-related or NVLink misconfig. Run a simple GPU local memcpy microbench and NCCL allreduce microbench to rule out NVLink/NCCL perf: 
```
cudaMemcpy bandwidth test (from sample apps)
nccl-tests/build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 512M -f 2 -g 4
```
If NCCL perf drops >10% vs lab, we investigate nvlink firmware or driver flags.

alex: Also collect perf counters for GPU SM utilization and memory BW: use nvidia-smi dmon or DCGM: 
```
nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1 -c 600 > dmon-sfo-rack-3-gpu-02.log
dcgmi hostengine --get-metrics > dcgm-metrics.json
```
Attach logs to ticket.

infra-bot: Perf suite results attached to INFRA-1124: latency and throughput runs completed. Flagged one node with nv_peer_mem missing and one with 5% token/sec regression.

sam: If regression persists after nv_peer_mem fix, we should roll driver rollback to previous known-good (533.x) in a canary and re-run. Any objections?

maya: +1 to canary rollback on a single rack, validate perf, then roll. We'll coordinate with platform to keep routing fallback ready.

alex: OK, action items: 1) todd to rebuild nvidia modules on gpu-07 and re-run microbench (ETA 20m). 2) maya to run NCCL/mem BW tests on all nodes (ETA 30m). 3) sam to pin capacity and re-run 10m throughput (ETA 1h). 4) infra-bot to attach logs and mark tickets. We'll reconvene in thread with final numbers and handoff notes. :thumbsup:

todd: On it. Posting dkms logs to INFRA-1123 once done.

maya: FYI I bumped MTU on the rack fabric to 9000 for the test pool — noted minor improvement in RPC latencies (~3-4ms).

alex: Great. If all green we'll update the regional bring-up runbook with the driver ver and the nv_peer_mem checklist. Also add an explicit step to disable autoscaler during perf validation.

todd: Rebuild complete on gpu-07, nv_peer_mem present now. Re-running perf-infer latency.

infra-bot: Update: latency run after nv_peer_mem fix -> p95 60ms (improved), tokens/sec 3250. Attached logs to INFRA-1123.

alex: Nice. Once sam finishes throughput and confirms regression gone we can mark SFO rack as validated and begin handoff to platform team.

sam: Throughput re-run results: 13.1k tokens/sec steady, p95 88ms. Within expected error margin. Closing INFRA-1124 as validated.

alex: Excellent — marking this thread for handoff notes. I'll update the runbook and ping platform for schedule. Thanks team.
